gaps.sentence: The players are gearing ___ for the final.
gaps.explanation: gear up for = prepare for a big event.

gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: Her essay stands ___ from the rest of the class.
gaps.explanation: stand out = be easy to notice, be better/different.

gaps.sentence: I fell ___ with my best friend over a silly remark.
gaps.explanation: fall out (with somebody) = have an argument and stop being friendly.

gaps.sentence: Sales figures have tailed ___ since the summer.
The negotiators refused to give ___ to the hijackers' demands.
gaps.explanation: give in (to) = stop arguing and accept; give up = quit.

gaps.sentence: The team was let ___ by its own supporters.
gaps.explanation: let somebody down = disappoint them by failing to help.

gaps.sentence: The bonus made up ___ all the overtime we had done.
gaps.explanation: make up FOR something = compensate for it.
